Listen to this article Share “Life is a poem. We have our different interpretations, all captured in words ” That is the perception of yours truly as practised over the decades. In fact, according to the globally acclaimed and multiple award – winning wordsmith, Prof. Akachi Ezeigbo, the Cross-Country Poetry Celebration (CCPC) with the theme, ‘Moments: Capturing Times with Words’, which was held in different states across the country, on Saturday October 17, 2026 equates to a “wonderful thing”, as she aptly expressed in her welcome address. Of great significance, was the brilliant and impactful handling of the particular event held at the popular St. Lawrence School, Ajasa Command, Lagos as hosted by renowned poet, Halima Abdulazeez, with the co-host, David Ararigho who organised Cross Country Poetry Initiative (C.C.P.I). Interestingly, this year’s edition marked the two years of consistent promotion of poetry, spoken word, and literary arts in the Ajasa Command community. As the theme suggests, the focus was on using poetry to document our reality. “Poetry is the epitome of all creative arts” -Adeyemi Adebiyi (former chairman of the Association of Nigerian Author’s, ANA, Lagos State Chapter) There cannot be poetry without words which some iconic poets refer to as the best ever expressed in different places. Such memorable words are expressed from deep emotions and feelings much of which remain timeless in spite of the cultural, socio-economic and political dynamics as people from different parts of the world express them. That perhaps, explains why Ezeigbo spoke extensively on the theme, emphasising the role of writers and poets as record keepers of society and urging young poets to document their own times authentically. On his part, the Guest Speaker, current President and founder of the Guild of Public Affairs Analyst of Nigeria (GPAAN), Ayo Oyoze Baje enjoined the students not to shy away from their talents, but take mentorship seriously, and be courageous enough to document their experiences. He provided insight into how one of his teachers in the English Language, then Miss Adeline Miller, later Mrs. Adeline Cripe (now of blessed memory) was able to highlight and hone his talent, especially in creative writing while a Form Three student at Ochaja Secondary School, in the then Kabba Province back in 1968. He went further to explain how he won the Complete Works of William Shakespeare in 1970 in Form Five class though as a student of science subjects. Years later, he was offered Poem of the Week column by the Nigerian Herald, beginning in 1978 and lasted for five years. He was fortunate to get one of his poems titled: ‘Mother at Childbirth’ published in a global anthology, “A Time to be Free” in 1998, and later won the Vanguard Poetry Award in 2003. And to cap it all, two of his poems including ‘Human Nature’ were published in another global anthology titled: ‘The Hybrid of Culture in 2025’. That got him a special invitation to Bangladesh to participate in the unveiling of ‘The Publication Festival of Swadhin Bangla Sahitya Prakashani including literary readings and cultural programmes on October 3, 2025. For all of the latest developments, he remains grateful to Halima Abdulazeez who provided the contacts and the impetus and told her students so. They should therefore, understand the way and manner of bringing out the poet in them by connecting with their heroes. Good enough, the 2026 edition provided the golden opportunity for the students Poetry Reading, the Spoken Word Performance and the Music Interlude. The Guest Poet, Yemi Adebiyi’s poem titled: ‘Nigeria We Hail Thee’ as ably represented by Obasi Mabel, touched on the nation’s history. It ended with: “Nigeria! You are not a headline/You are a heartbeat/ And as long as the drum beats in us../ This story is not finished’/” On her part, Halima read her poignant poem titled: ‘The violin and the Savior’ beginning with: ‘Here to save humans from the ashes of ruin/ The strings bear witness,/each confessing to a stiff dissent/ against trading souls for a cent./. It ends with /Then, the violin must cracks through the shifting sands and the broken hymns./To awaken humans from slumber/.” That brought to the fore, the profile of Sir Eriata Oribhabor as read by Halima.. His support for youth and the birth of what Poets in Nigeria that later metamorphosed into Cross Country Poetry Celebration was duly acknowledged. The team that delivered this year’s CCPI, the president, Mohammed Idris Evuti and the secretary, Othman. The cohost David Ararigho thrilled the audience with the miming and dancing segments of the event. David Adoga a student of St. Lawrence Greater Heights School emerged as the best in the individual rendition of poems while his school placed second behind M and B School, with the three others, Top Set Vision College, Prince of Glory College, and Dah Best College placed third, fourth and fifth in that order. That was as announced by the Panel of Judges made up of Nwaosisike Monica Judge, Obasi Mabel and Okolie Christopher. The lasting lessons from the event include the need to catch our talents young, encourage and support them as the sponsors, Adeosun, Proprietress of St. Lawrence School, the PEN Nigeria Young Writers Committee, the President of LITACO Awele Ilusanmi, Adeyemi Adebiyi, Hajia Lawal Mudirat, Davy Fidel have done. Not left out is the founder of FST Stitches, who offered her time and resources to cover the entire event, as Halima expressed her gratitude. All these attest to the fact, as rightly put by one on the poets in attendance, Okorie Christopher that: “Poetry is not just words arranged in lines./Poetry is the music of the soul./. He urges us therefore, to: “Let us read poetry. Let us write poetry. Let us teach our children poetry, so that they will not only learn how to make a living, but also learn how to live”.
